macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global stocks steadied as oil retreated after fresh U.S.-Iran tensions
items.summary: U.S. stock futures and European shares recovered from earlier weakness as oil prices eased, even as investors continued to weigh renewed geopolitical risk from fresh U.S. strikes on Iran. Reuters said Asian markets also advanced, but gains were capped by higher oil and renewed inflation concerns.

items.title: Oil prices and inflation worries remain a key market driver
items.summary: Reuters reported that oil rose after the U.S. launched fresh strikes against Iran, reviving fears about disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz and pushing inflation expectations higher. The same report said the U.S. dollar stayed firm as safe-haven demand increased and rate-hike bets rose.

items.title: Japan's 10-year government bond yield hit a 30-year high
items.summary: Reuters reported that the benchmark 10-year Japanese Government Bond yield reached its highest level in three decades as higher oil prices renewed inflation concerns. The move also reflected investor caution about Japan's fiscal outlook.

items.title: Fed caution weighed on Australian shares
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Australian shares wobbled as caution from the Federal Reserve tempered optimism from lower oil prices. The same market roundup highlighted ongoing pressure in the yen and mixed trading across Asian markets.

items.title: OPEC+ agreed to raise output targets again
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that seven countries in the OPEC+ alliance agreed to increase combined oil output by 188,000 barrels per day in August. The move adds supply pressure to a market already reacting to Middle East tensions and volatile crude prices.

items.title: PepsiCo posted stronger revenue but warned on consumer demand pressure
items.summary: Yahoo Finance said PepsiCo's second-quarter net revenue rose 6.4% to $24.2 billion, helped by stronger-than-expected results. The company also cited weaker North American demand as consumers tightened budgets due to broader economic concerns.

items.title: CNBC highlighted premarket stock moves in major names
items.summary: CNBC reported notable premarket activity in stocks including AstraZeneca, PepsiCo, Salesforce, and Levi's. Its market coverage also said chip stocks were rebounding and U.S. Treasury yields steadied after a prior spike.

items.title: SpaceX is set to join the Nasdaq-100
items.summary: CNN reported that SpaceX will officially join the Nasdaq-100 index, creating new exposure for investors and likely triggering automatic buying from index funds. The move underscores continued index-driven flows in large-cap U.S. equity markets.

items.title: IMF cut its 2026 global growth forecast
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the IMF lowered its 2026 world growth forecast to 3 percent, citing fallout from the Iran war. The fund said artificial intelligence-related demand may partly offset the energy shock.

items.title: China's producer prices rose again, adding to global inflation concerns
items.summary: Reuters said China's producer price inflation rose for a fourth straight month to its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also extended gains. The data reinforced concerns that cost pressures remain elevated for manufacturers.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin traded mixed, with reports showing moves around the low-to-mid $60,000s
items.summary: Several crypto news outlets reported Bitcoin near $62,240 to $63,589 over the past day, while other market coverage showed it struggling to hold support around $62,500. The variation reflects rapid intraday volatility rather than a single stable price level.

items.title: Shiba Inu surged sharply in a mystery rally
items.summary: CoinDesk reported SHIB rose about 35% to 36% in 24 hours, adding roughly $1 billion in market value without a clear project announcement. The move stood out because it outpaced the broader dog-token complex and came with unusually heavy trading volume.

items.title: The broader crypto market saw leveraged liquidations and weakness
items.summary: Market coverage said the crypto market fell about 1.4% and more than $420 million in leveraged positions were liquidated over the last 24 hours. Ether also dropped about 5% in one report amid continued caution and ETF-related pressure.

items.title: U.S. crypto regulation moved closer to a major CLARITY vote
items.summary: Crypto.news reported that Paul Grewal exited Coinbase’s legal leadership before a key CLARITY Act vote, and that the Trump White House rejected SEC-snub claims ahead of the showdown. The coverage points to a consequential U.S. policy moment for the industry.

items.title: Hong Kong tightened crypto platform security rules
items.summary: crypto.news reported that Hong Kong’s SFC is forcing crypto platforms to stop using SMS authentication, a move aimed at improving account security. This is a notable operational compliance change for exchanges serving the region.

items.title: The European Union may revisit MiCA to address stablecoin issuers
items.summary: Gate and Newsbit reported that EU diplomats are preparing to reopen the MiCA rulebook, potentially in 2027, to regulate non-EU stablecoin issuers more directly. If confirmed, this would be a significant extension of Europe’s crypto framework.

items.title: SWIFT expanded blockchain-based payments testing
items.summary: Multiple reports said SWIFT is launching or expanding blockchain payment trials, including cross-border payment efforts with participating banks. This is one of the most important traditional-finance blockchain developments in the current news cycle.

items.title: XRP rose on a SWIFT-related payments story
items.summary: crypto.news reported that XRP gained after SWIFT tapped Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments. The move was presented as a notable real-world payments development tied to Ripple’s ecosystem.

items.title: The Ethereum Foundation cut spending and staff
items.summary: Coin Insider and TodayOnChain reported that the Ethereum Foundation will cut its budget by 40% and headcount by 20%, shifting toward an endowment-style spending model. The change signals a sharper focus on core protocol development and treasury discipline.

items.title: A Cardano wallet vulnerability led to losses at SecondFi
items.summary: TodayOnChain reported that SecondFi identified an address-level vulnerability in its Cardano wallet software that caused unauthorized fund outflows and significant user losses. The report also said the project faces more than $20 million in losses tied to the flaw.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across apps and files, expanding its push into professional AI tools and enterprise automation.

items.title: Meta opens preview access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark 1.1 model, a new version aimed at stronger coding performance and broader competition with rival model providers.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live voice models for real-time speech
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously, indicating continued investment in real-time conversational AI.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched Grok 4.5, which it described as its most intelligent model yet and optimized for coding and agent-style workflows.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its oversight body, underscoring governance and mission-alignment concerns around frontier AI development.

items.title: Meta plans to manufacture an AI chip starting in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to begin making an AI chip in September as part of a broader effort to expand computing capacity and reduce infrastructure constraints.

items.title: Meta announces first data center in Canada
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, adding to its rapid infrastructure expansion to support AI workloads and global computing demand.

items.title: Micron commits more than $250 billion to U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest over $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging AI-driven demand for memory chips and domestic manufacturing priorities.

items.title: China's AI model ecosystem gains ground
items.summary: Coverage this week highlighted that Chinese AI startups such as Z.ai, Moonshot, and Alibaba are rapidly closing the capability gap with leading Western models while pushing more open and cheaper alternatives.

items.title: AI research points to broader progress in materials, medicine, and brain-like systems
items.summary: Recent science reporting highlighted machine learning helping discover new superconductors, improving blood-cell analysis for disease detection, and producing more brain-like AI behavior with less training data.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox cuts deepen as Microsoft reportedly sells off or spins out multiple studios
items.summary: Microsoft’s gaming division is undergoing another major restructuring, with reports that Double Fine and Compulsion Games are going independent while Ninja Theory and Undead Labs are being sold. The move follows broader Xbox job cuts affecting roughly 20% of the gaming division.

items.title: IO Interactive closes one studio and lays off staff after Xbox funding loss
items.summary: IO Interactive, the developer behind Hitman and 007: First Light, is shutting down one of its studios and laying off an undisclosed number of employees after Xbox reportedly withdrew funding for an upcoming project. The company says its next franchise will continue.

items.title: Capcom moves up Onimusha: Way of the Sword release date
items.summary: Capcom has advanced the launch of Onimusha: Way of the Sword to September 4, earlier than the previously planned September 25 release. The game is one of the most notable recent release-date changes in the industry.

items.title: Microsoft says Game Pass growth has fallen far short of expectations
items.summary: Xbox leadership has acknowledged that Game Pass has not grown to the level Microsoft previously projected, with reports saying the service is tens of millions of subscribers below target. The admission marks a notable shift in Microsoft’s gaming strategy.

items.title: Sony says new PlayStation games will be digital-only starting in 2028
items.summary: Sony has confirmed that it is ending physical discs for future PlayStation games, with new releases after January 2028 set to be digital-only. The announcement has sparked renewed debate about ownership and preservation.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports launch on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 are now available on PlayStation consoles, bringing two classic entries to current hardware. IGN notes that the ports come at a high price.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced sets new franchise peak on Steam
items.summary: Ubisoft’s Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced has reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, reportedly the highest peak for any game in the series. The strong start suggests significant interest in the remake.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour shutdown
items.summary: Nintendo will shut down Mario Kart Tour this September after seven years of service, and the company says it will not offer an offline version. The decision adds to concerns about long-term access to mobile games.

items.title: Subnautica 2 tops 5 million copies sold ahead of early access update
items.summary: PC Gamer reports that Subnautica 2 has sold 5 million copies ahead of its first early access update, called Adaptive Measures. The milestone underscores the series’ continued commercial strength.

items.title: Mortal Shell 2 gets a release window
items.summary: Yahoo Tech reports that Mortal Shell 2 now has a release date set for August. The announcement is one of the notable new-game release updates from the last day.
